title: The Two Pots

full_text:
Two cooking pots—one fashioned of sturdy hammered brass, and the other made of delicate earthen clay—were swept from a kitchen shelf by a sudden flood and floated together down the swollen river.

The Brass Pot called out cheerfully to his clay companion: "Fear nothing, neighbor! Float close beside me; I will protect you and keep you safe from the crashing waves!"

The wise Earthen Pot paddled backward with all his might and replied:

"I thank you for your generous goodwill, friend, but I beg you to keep as far from me as possible! If a rock strikes me, I am shattered; but if you strike me in friendship, I am equally shattered to pieces. Whether we meet in battle or in friendly collision, the clay pot must always be the loser!"
moral: The weak must keep a safe distance from the strong; collision brings ruin to the fragile.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Two Pots"?
options: Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
